e-11372.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Sphere
e-11372.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2=4.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R (y-z)\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2} \:\textrm{d}V
$$
e-11372.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
\iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \, \mathrm{d}V = 
\iiint\limits_{\Delta} \, f(\rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \rho\cos\phi) \:  \rho^2\sin\phi \: \mathrm{d}\rho \, \mathrm{d}\theta \, \mathrm{d}\phi.
$$

If $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x = \rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \qquad
y = \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \qquad 
z = \rho\cos\phi
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $2$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
\Delta = \left\{ (\rho, \theta, \phi) \, : \, 0 \leq \rho \leq 2, \: 0 \leq \theta \lt 2\pi, \: 0 \leq \phi \leq \pi \right\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=(y-z)\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(y-z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

e-12409.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Part-Sphere
e-12409.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2=4$ for $y \leq 0.$ 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R \dfrac{1}{x^2+y^2+z^2} \:\textrm{d}V
$$
e-12409.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
\iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \, \mathrm{d}V = 
\iiint\limits_{\Delta} \, f(\rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \rho\cos\phi) \:  \rho^2\sin\phi \: \mathrm{d}\rho \, \mathrm{d}\theta \, \mathrm{d}\phi.
$$

If $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x = \rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \qquad
y = \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \qquad 
z = \rho\cos\phi
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $2$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/4689af5de2bb93606060ff95ee2f2af1d34206c3ab89be8f854108c855a00aa3.png)

  

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
\Delta = \left\{ (\rho, \theta, \phi) \, : \, 0 \leq \rho \leq 2, \: \pi \leq \theta \leq 2\pi, \: 0 \leq \phi \leq \pi \right\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\dfrac{1}{x^2+y^2+z^2}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=9. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rzx2+y2+z2dV

a
∫0π∫02π∫03ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫03ρ3sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫02π∫02π∫03ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫02π∫09ρ3sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫02π∫02π∫03ρ4cos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit

decision.explanation: Using z=ρ cosϕ, √(x²+y²+z²)=ρ, and dV=ρ² sinϕ dρ dθ dϕ gives the integrand ρ⁴ cosϕ sinϕ. The sphere has radius 3, with 0≤ρ≤3, 0≤θ≤2π, and 0≤ϕ≤π, so option a is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
after.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $3$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 3,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=9. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rzx2+y2+z2dV

a
∫0π∫02π∫03ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫03ρ3sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫02π∫02π∫03ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫02π∫09ρ3sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫02π∫02π∫03ρ4cos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 3 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤3,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=zx2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρcos⁡ϕ⋅ρ=ρ2cos⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rzx2+y2+z2dV=∭Δρ2cos⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫03ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

content.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Sphere
content.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
content.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $3$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 3,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=5. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R(x+z)x2+y2+z2dV

a
∫0π∫02π∫05ρ3sin⁡ϕcos⁡θ(sin⁡ϕ+1)dρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫05ρ4(sin⁡ϕ+cos⁡θ)dρdθdϕ
c
∫02π∫02π∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+sin⁡θcos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
d
∫02π∫02π∫05ρ3sin⁡ϕ(cos2⁡θ+cos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫02π∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+cos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
Submit

decision.explanation: Substitute x=ρ cosθ sinϕ, z=ρ cosϕ, and √(x²+y²+z²)=ρ. Multiplying by the Jacobian ρ² sinϕ gives ρ⁴ sinϕ(cosθ sinϕ+cosϕ). The bounds are 0≤ρ≤√5, 0≤θ≤2π, and 0≤ϕ≤π, matching option e.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=5.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}(x+z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
after.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $\sqrt{5}$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{5},\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=(x+z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(x+z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{5}}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=5. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R(x+z)x2+y2+z2dV

a
∫0π∫02π∫05ρ3sin⁡ϕcos⁡θ(sin⁡ϕ+1)dρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫05ρ4(sin⁡ϕ+cos⁡θ)dρdθdϕ
c
∫02π∫02π∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+sin⁡θcos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
d
∫02π∫02π∫05ρ3sin⁡ϕ(cos2⁡θ+cos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫02π∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+cos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 5 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤5,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=(x+z)x2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+ρcos⁡ϕ)⋅ρ=ρ2(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+cos⁡ϕ)

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R(x+z)x2+y2+z2dV=∭Δρ2(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+cos⁡ϕ)⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+cos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ.

content.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Sphere
content.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=5.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}(x+z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
content.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $\sqrt{5}$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{5},\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=(x+z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(x+z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{5}}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 3
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=19. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Ryzx2+y2dV

a
∫02π∫02π∫03ρ2sin2⁡ϕcos2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫01/9ρ3sin⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫02π∫02π∫01/3ρ3sin2⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫02π∫01/9ρ2cos⁡θcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫02π∫01/3ρ2sin⁡θcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit

decision.explanation: Since yz=ρ² sinθ sinϕ cosϕ and x²+y²=ρ² sin²ϕ, multiplying their ratio by the Jacobian ρ² sinϕ gives ρ² sinθ cosϕ. The sphere has radius 1/3, with 0≤θ≤2π and 0≤ϕ≤π. Thus option e is correct; the undefined values on the z-axis do not affect the integral.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=\frac{1}{9}.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
after.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $\frac{1}{3}$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \frac{1}{3},\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1/3}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=19. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Ryzx2+y2dV

a
∫02π∫02π∫03ρ2sin2⁡ϕcos2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫01/9ρ3sin⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫02π∫02π∫01/3ρ3sin2⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫02π∫01/9ρ2cos⁡θcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫02π∫01/3ρ2sin⁡θcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 13 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤13,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=yzx2+y2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ⋅ρcos⁡ϕ(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2+(ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2=ρ2sin⁡θsin⁡ϕcos⁡ϕρ2sin2⁡ϕ(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)=sin⁡θcos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Ryzx2+y2dV=∭Δsin⁡θcos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫01/3ρ2sin⁡θcos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

content.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Sphere
content.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=\frac{1}{9}.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
content.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $\frac{1}{3}$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \frac{1}{3},\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1/3}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Using x=ρ cosθ sinϕ and y=ρ sinθ sinϕ, the ratio xy/(x²+y²+z²) becomes cosθ sinθ sin²ϕ. Multiplication by the Jacobian ρ² sinϕ gives ρ² cosθ sinθ sin³ϕ. The radius is 5, with θ from 0 to 2π and ϕ from 0 to π, matching option d.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=25.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{xy}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
after.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $5$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 5,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{xy}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{xy}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{5}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

b

c

EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 5 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤5,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=xyx2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ⋅ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕρ2=cos⁡θsin⁡θsin2⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rxyx2+y2+z2dV=∭Δcos⁡θsin⁡θsin2⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫05ρ2cos⁡θsin⁡θsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

content.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Sphere
content.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=25.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{xy}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
content.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $5$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 5,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{xy}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{xy}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{5}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

b
∫0π∫02π∫016ρ3sin⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫0π∫02π∫04ρ4cos⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ

decision.explanation: Since y=ρ sinθ sinϕ and √(x²+y²+z²)=ρ, multiplying by dV=ρ² sinϕ dρ dθ dϕ gives ρ⁴ sinθ sin²ϕ. The sphere has radius 4, with 0≤θ≤2π and 0≤ϕ≤π, matching option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=16.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
after.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $4$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 4,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{4}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=16. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Ryx2+y2+z2dV

a
∫0π∫02π∫04ρ4sin⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫02π∫016ρ3sin⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫0π∫02π∫04ρ4cos⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫02π∫02π∫04ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫02π∫02π∫016ρ3cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 4 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤4,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=yx2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ=ρ2sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Ryx2+y2+z2dV=∭Δρ2sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫04ρ4sin⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

content.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Sphere
content.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=16.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
content.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $4$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 4,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{4}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=2 for y≤0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rzx2+y2dV

a
 ∫0π∫π2π∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫π2π∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
 ∫0π∫0π∫02ρ2sin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
 ∫0π∫0π∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫π/23π/2∫02ρ2sin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit

decision.explanation: Here z=ρ cosϕ and √(x²+y²)=ρ sinϕ. Multiplying by the Jacobian ρ² sinϕ gives ρ⁴ cosϕ sin²ϕ. The radius is √2, and y≤0 requires π≤θ≤2π, while 0≤ϕ≤π. This matches option b.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2$ for $y\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
after.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/6f35be4fd6773149597ea8a9dc8dd234e068da3f0fd3b2df32d11c61521bed75.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{2},\,\pi \le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ} \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=2 for y≤0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rzx2+y2dV

a
 ∫0π∫π2π∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
∫0π∫π2π∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
 ∫0π∫0π∫02ρ2sin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
 ∫0π∫0π∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫π/23π/2∫02ρ2sin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-half of the sphere of radius 2 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤2,π≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=zx2+y2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρcos⁡ϕ(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2+(ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2=ρcos⁡ϕρ2cos2⁡θsin2⁡ϕ+ρ2sin2⁡θsin2⁡ϕ=ρcos⁡ϕρ2sin2⁡ϕ(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)=ρcos⁡ϕρ2sin2⁡ϕ=ρ2cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rzx2+y2dV=∭Δρ2cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫π2π∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

content.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Part-Sphere
content.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2$ for $y\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
content.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/6f35be4fd6773149597ea8a9dc8dd234e068da3f0fd3b2df32d11c61521bed75.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{2},\,\pi \le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ} \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=25 for x≤0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R(x2+y2+z2)dV

a
 ∫0π∫0π∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫0π∫π3π/2∫05ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
 ∫0π∫π/23π/2∫05ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫π/23π/2∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫0π∫0π/2∫05ρ3sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit

decision.explanation: The integrand is ρ², and the Jacobian is ρ² sinϕ, giving ρ⁴ sinϕ. The sphere has radius 5. Since x=ρ cosθ sinϕ≤0, take π/2≤θ≤3π/2, with 0≤ϕ≤π. These bounds and integrand match option d.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=25$ for $x\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}V
$$
after.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $5$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/2f5814367e44117edbfee704207ef48da2fdb5fa56cbb76b35dd4b0b1ac336ca.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 5,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{5}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=25 for x≤0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R(x2+y2+z2)dV

a
 ∫0π∫0π∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫0π∫π3π/2∫05ρ4cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
 ∫0π∫π/23π/2∫05ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
∫0π∫π/23π/2∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫0π∫0π/2∫05ρ3sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-half of the sphere of radius 5 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤5,π2≤θ≤3π2,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=x2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρ2

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R(x2+y2+z2)dV=∭Δρ2⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫π/23π/2∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $5$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/2f5814367e44117edbfee704207ef48da2fdb5fa56cbb76b35dd4b0b1ac336ca.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 5,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{5}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}2x({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}V
$$

Question 8
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=16 for x≤0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R2x(x2+y2)dV

a
 ∫0π∫π/23π/2∫042ρ4sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫π/23π/2∫π/2π∫042ρ5sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫0π∫π/23π/2∫042ρ5cos⁡θsin4⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
 ∫0π∫π2π∫042ρ5cos⁡θsin4⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫0π∫π2π∫042ρ4cos2⁡ϕsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit

decision.explanation: Substituting x=ρ cosθ sinϕ and x²+y²=ρ² sin²ϕ, then multiplying by the Jacobian ρ² sinϕ, gives 2ρ⁵ cosθ sin⁴ϕ. The radius is 4, and x≤0 requires π/2≤θ≤3π/2, with 0≤ϕ≤π. This matches option c.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=16$ for $x\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}2x({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}V
$$
after.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $4$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/8c803dbf5bcf6c2ece6c1c8352f96da1c88734ca1d792dd05593ac8c11527b2b.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 4,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=2x({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ((\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}) \\  & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ({\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) \\  & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ({\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )) \\  & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ({\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) \\  & =2{\rho }^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2x({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}2{\rho }^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{4}2{\rho }^{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{4}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}

Question 8
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=16 for x≤0. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R2x(x2+y2)dV

a
 ∫0π∫π/23π/2∫042ρ4sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫π/23π/2∫π/2π∫042ρ5sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
∫0π∫π/23π/2∫042ρ5cos⁡θsin4⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
 ∫0π∫π2π∫042ρ5cos⁡θsin4⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫0π∫π2π∫042ρ4cos2⁡ϕsin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-half of the sphere of radius 4 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤4,π2≤θ≤3π2,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=2x(x2+y2):

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=2ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ((ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2+(ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2)=2ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ(ρ2cos2⁡θsin2⁡ϕ+ρ2sin2⁡θsin2⁡ϕ)=2ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ(ρ2sin2⁡ϕ(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ))=2ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ(ρ2sin2⁡ϕ)=2ρ3cos⁡θsin3⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R2x(x2+y2)dV=∭Δ2ρ3cos⁡θsin3⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫π/23π/2∫042ρ5cos⁡θsin4⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
